answers.q1: Yarn 1 (classic), pinned by the root package.json "packageManager": "yarn@1.22.22" in a Yarn workspaces monorepo (Node 20.x per CI). Install with: yarn install
answers.q2: yarn test:all (runs test:typecheck, test:code, test:other, then test:app --watch=false). The Vitest-only run is: yarn test:app --watch=false
answers.q4: yarn test:other && yarn test:code && yarn test:typecheck (CI runs these after yarn install; test:other is prettier --list-different, test:code is eslint --max-warnings=0 --ext .js,.ts,.tsx ., test:typecheck is tsc)
answers.q5: Yes. packages/excalidraw/types/ (generated declarations, gitignored); build outputs such as dist/, build/, dev-dist/, coverage/, and public/workbox (generated by the PWA build); packages/excalidraw/locales/*.json except en.json, which is the Crowdin source (crowdin.yml syncs the other locales from Crowdin, so they should not be hand-edited).

q1.reason: Yarn classic with `yarn install` from the root matches the accept criterion.

q2.reason: `yarn test:all` is an accepted superset and `yarn test:app --watch=false` is the accepted one-shot form.

q3.reason: `yarn test:app --watch=false packages/element/tests/bounds.test.ts` is equivalent to the accepted form, with the file filter still applied and the flag order immaterial.

q4.reason: Gives yarn test:other, test:code and test:typecheck, exactly what CI runs.

q5.reason: Names the non-en locale files, build output dirs (dist/, build/, dev-dist/) and the generated types dir, which match the accept criteria with no rejected items.
